summary: New sense 2: (Detrans.) durch Rauch verschmutzen, verrußen (mit mən-)
rationale: House subjects, smoke as source/cause and subsequent whitewashing distinguish soot-blackening from corrosion or metaphorical inactivity. One clear attestation.

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Ab bote, d kmizangri mad dəxone, mam mədone, kəmšarbəṭənne. W makkinat hwalle. Qamayto bi maknəšto saymiwo.
data.translation: Father Brahim: Houses which become blackened from the smoke, from the hearths, they whitewash them. And machines came to be used. At first they did it with a broom.

rationale: First smoke-soiling sense; smoke cause and whitewashing response are explicit in the Turoyo. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: Retain the entry's I and Detransitive labels for mzangri; no external agent or patient object is expressed.
The lack of work supplies the basis of the bodily-rust metaphor in the Turoyo itself. A separate inactivity sense is unnecessary: record the extension beside existing Detransitive rosten/einrosten.
The entry has no numbered active senses and no contextual example of literal metal rusting. Do not invent either from the loan etymology or isolated Infectum base.
The longer source adds an audience interjection koḥayki and a no-work explanation; neither warrants duplication of the existing 73/429 example.
The Turoyo combines ab bote with mad dəxone and kəmšarbəṭənne, securing smoke-soiling independently of the machine blackened.

This is a distinct material process from rusting: no metallic substrate or oxidation is stated. It therefore receives Detransitive sense 2, while round 1’s figurative inactivity remains an extension of 1.
Preserve inherited I and Detransitive labels; no causer-object active form is attested.
Can a native speaker provide a literal metal-rusting context for comparison? The supplied textual example supports only figurative hands rusting through disuse.
Does zngr cover other kinds of surface grime or specifically smoke deposits in this dialect? One house/whitewashing passage cannot determine the full extension.

rationale: rostetet is an erroneous verb ending here. The quoted k-mizangər is singular Infectum and the gloss is einrosten, giving rostet ein.

summary: Hands are figuratively rusted through inactivity; the following me zawno lo šaġənno explicitly links the state to not having worked. This is the only contextual rust example supplied.
